source.text: וַיֵּ֥רֶד שִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן תִּמְנָ֑תָה וַיַּ֥רְא אִשָּׁ֛ה בְּתִמְנָ֖תָה מִבְּנ֥וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And went down Samson to Timnah, and he saw a woman in Timnah from [the] daughters of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And Samson went down to Timnah, and he saw a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines.
en.B: Samson went down to Timnah, and in Timnah he noticed one of the young Philistine women.
en.R: Samson went down to the town of Timnah. While he was there, he saw a young Philistine woman.

sw.L: Naye Samsoni akashuka mpaka Timna, akamwona mwanamke huko Timna katika binti za Wafilisti.
sw.B: Samsoni alishuka mpaka Timna, na huko Timna akamwona msichana mmoja wa Kifilisti.
sw.R: Samsoni alishuka mpaka mji wa Timna. Alipokuwa huko, alimwona msichana mmoja wa Kifilisti.

es.L: Y descendió Sansón a Timnat, y vio en Timnat a una mujer de las hijas de los filisteos.
es.B: Sansón descendió a Timnat, y allí, en Timnat, se fijó en una joven filistea.
es.R: Sansón bajó al pueblo de Timnat. Mientras estaba allí, vio a una joven filistea.

fr.L: Et Samson descendit à Timna, et il vit à Timna une femme d’entre les filles des Philistins.
fr.B: Samson descendit à Timna, et là il remarqua une des jeunes Philistines.
fr.R: Samson est descendu à la ville de Timna. Pendant qu’il était là-bas, il a vu une jeune Philistine.

vi.L: Sam-sôn đi xuống Thim-na, và ông thấy một người phụ nữ ở Thim-na trong số các con gái người Phi-li-tin.
vi.B: Sam-sôn đi xuống Thim-na, và tại Thim-na ông để ý thấy một thiếu nữ Phi-li-tin.
vi.R: Sam-sôn đi xuống thành Thim-na. Khi ở đó, ông thấy một thiếu nữ Phi-li-tin.

ko.L: 삼손이 딤나로 내려가서, 딤나에서 블레셋 사람들의 딸들 가운데 한 여자를 보았다.
ko.B: 삼손이 딤나로 내려갔다가, 거기에서 블레셋의 젊은 여자 하나를 눈여겨보았다.
ko.R: 삼손이 딤나 성으로 내려갔다. 그는 거기에서 블레셋의 젊은 여자 하나를 보았다.

decisions.choice: went down to Timnah: from the hill country down into the valley
decisions.reason: Samson's home was at Zorah and Eshtaol in the hills (13:2, 25). Timnah lay lower, toward the plain, on the border between Judah and Dan (Joshua 15:10; 19:43), so the story speaks of going "down" to it and "up" from it (verse 2).

decisions.choice: the daughters of the Philistines: young Philistine women
decisions.reason: "Daughters" of a people means the women of that people, here young women of marriageable age. The phrase sets the scene: the woman Samson wants is a Philistine, from the people who ruled Israel at this time (13:1).

decisions.choice: the town of Timnah
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" so that a new reader knows Timnah is a place.

decisions.choice: "Timna"
decisions.reason: For Judges 14-15: the town keeps the French form of Genesis 38 in this translation.

decisions.choice: "Thim-na" for Timnah; "người Phi-li-tin" for the Philistines
decisions.reason: Philistines as the Joshua–Ruth terms note; Timnah takes the usual Protestant spelling and stays the same through Samson's story.

source.text: וַיַּ֗עַל וַיַּגֵּד֙ לְאָבִ֣יו וּלְאִמּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִשָּׁ֛ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְתִמְנָ֖תָה מִבְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְעַתָּ֕ה קְחוּ־אוֹתָ֥הּ לִּ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went up and told his father and his mother, and he said, a woman I have seen in Timnah from [the] daughters of [the] Philistines; and now take her for me as a wife.

en.L: And he went up and told his father and his mother, and he said, "A woman I have seen in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines; and now take her for me as a wife."
en.B: He came back up and told his father and mother, "I have seen a woman in Timnah, one of the young Philistine women. Now get her for me as my wife."
en.R: When he came back home, he told his father and mother, "I saw a young Philistine woman in Timnah. Now go and arrange for me to marry her."

sw.L: Naye akapanda, akawaambia baba yake na mama yake, akasema, "Mwanamke nimemwona huko Timna katika binti za Wafilisti; basi sasa mnipatie awe mke wangu."
sw.B: Alipanda kurudi, akawaambia baba yake na mama yake, "Nimemwona mwanamke huko Timna, mmoja wa wasichana wa Kifilisti. Sasa mnipatie awe mke wangu."
sw.R: Aliporudi nyumbani, aliwaambia baba yake na mama yake, "Nimemwona msichana wa Kifilisti huko Timna. Sasa nendeni mkapange niweze kumwoa."

es.L: Y subió y [lo] contó a su padre y a su madre, y dijo: «Una mujer he visto en Timnat, de las hijas de los filisteos; y ahora {{plural_you:tómenmela|tomádmela}} por mujer».
es.B: Volvió a subir y se lo contó a su padre y a su madre: «He visto en Timnat a una mujer, una de las jóvenes filisteas. Ahora {{plural_you:consíganmela|conseguídmela}} como esposa».
es.R: Cuando volvió a casa, les dijo a su padre y a su madre: «Vi en Timnat a una joven filistea. Ahora {{plural_you:vayan|id}} a arreglar mi casamiento con ella».

fr.L: Et il remonta et le raconta à son père et à sa mère, et il dit : « Une femme, j’[en] ai vu une à Timna, d’entre les filles des Philistins ; et maintenant, prenez-la-moi pour femme. »
fr.B: Il remonta chez lui et dit à son père et à sa mère : « J’ai vu à Timna une femme, une des jeunes Philistines. Maintenant, obtenez-la-moi pour épouse. »
fr.R: Quand il est rentré chez lui, il a dit à son père et à sa mère : « J’ai vu une jeune Philistine à Timna. Maintenant, allez arranger mon mariage avec elle. »

vi.L: Ông đi lên và nói với cha mẹ mình: "Con đã thấy một người phụ nữ ở Thim-na trong số các con gái người Phi-li-tin; vậy bây giờ xin cha mẹ cưới nàng cho con làm vợ."
vi.B: Ông trở lên nhà và nói với cha mẹ: "Con đã thấy một thiếu nữ Phi-li-tin ở Thim-na. Bây giờ xin cha mẹ cưới cô ấy về làm vợ cho con."
vi.R: Khi về nhà, ông nói với cha mẹ: "Con đã thấy một thiếu nữ Phi-li-tin ở Thim-na. Bây giờ xin cha mẹ đi lo việc cưới cô ấy cho con."

ko.L: 그가 올라와서 자기 아버지와 어머니에게 알리며 말했다. "제가 딤나에서 블레셋 사람들의 딸들 가운데 한 여자를 보았습니다. 이제 그 여자를 저에게 아내로 데려와 주십시오."
ko.B: 그는 집으로 올라와서 아버지와 어머니에게 말했다. "제가 딤나에서 블레셋의 젊은 여자 하나를 보았습니다. 이제 그 여자를 제 아내로 맞아 주십시오."
ko.R: 삼손은 집에 돌아와서 아버지와 어머니에게 말했다. "제가 딤나에서 블레셋의 젊은 여자를 보았습니다. 이제 가셔서 제가 그 여자와 결혼할 수 있게 해 주십시오."

decisions.choice: take her for me as a wife: the parents arrange the marriage
decisions.reason: Marriages were arranged between families, and the groom's family made the agreement with the bride's father, often with a payment to him (Genesis 34:4, 8-12; Exodus 22:15-16). The command is plural: Samson tells both parents to make the arrangements.

decisions.choice: A woman I have seen: the woman comes first for emphasis
decisions.reason: Samson puts "a woman" at the head of his sentence. What he has seen is what drives him, a theme of the chapter (verses 1, 3, 7).

decisions.choice: go and arrange for me to marry her
decisions.reason: "Take her for me" means "arrange the marriage for me". Readable says so, so that it does not sound as if the parents are to fetch the woman by force.

decisions.choice: Samson says "cha mẹ" and "con"; his parents call him "con"
decisions.reason: As the Genesis note sets for parents and children.

decisions.choice: Samson speaks to his parents in the formal polite style (합쇼체); they answer him in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for parent and child.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֜וֹ אָבִ֣יו וְאִמּ֗וֹ הַאֵין֩ בִּבְנ֨וֹת אַחֶ֤יךָ וּבְכָל־עַמִּי֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּֽי־אַתָּ֤ה הוֹלֵךְ֙ לָקַ֣חַת אִשָּׁ֔ה מִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים הָעֲרֵלִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֤וֹן אֶל־אָבִיו֙ אוֹתָ֣הּ קַֽח־לִ֔י כִּֽי־הִ֖יא יָשְׁרָ֥ה בְעֵינָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him his father and his mother, [is there] not among [the] daughters of your brothers and among all my people a woman, that you [are] going to take a wife from the Philistines the uncircumcised? And said Samson to his father, her take for me, for she [is] right in my eyes.

en.L: And his father and his mother said to him, "Is there no woman among the daughters of your brothers, or among all my people, that you are going to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" And Samson said to his father, "Her take for me, for she is right in my eyes."
en.B: His father and mother said to him, "Is there not a woman among your relatives or anywhere among my people? Must you go and take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" But Samson said to his father, "Get her for me. She is the one who looks right to me."
en.R: His father and mother said to him, "Is there no woman among our relatives or among all our people? Why do you have to go and marry one of the Philistines? They are not even circumcised!" But Samson said to his father, "Get her for me. She is the one I like."

sw.L: Nao baba yake na mama yake wakamwambia, "Je, hakuna mwanamke katika binti za ndugu zako, wala katika watu wangu wote, hata wewe uende kutwaa mke kwa Wafilisti wasiotahiriwa?" Naye Samsoni akamwambia baba yake, "Huyo nipatie, kwa maana yeye ni sawa machoni pangu."
sw.B: Baba yake na mama yake walimwambia, "Je, hakuna mwanamke kati ya jamaa zako, au popote kati ya watu wangu? Je, ni lazima uende kutwaa mke kwa Wafilisti wasiotahiriwa?" Lakini Samsoni alimwambia baba yake, "Nipatie huyo. Yeye ndiye anayefaa machoni pangu."
sw.R: Baba yake na mama yake walimwambia, "Je, hakuna mwanamke kati ya jamaa zetu au kati ya watu wetu wote? Kwa nini ni lazima uende kuoa mmoja wa Wafilisti? Wao hata hawajatahiriwa!" Lakini Samsoni alimwambia baba yake, "Nipatie huyo. Yeye ndiye ninayempenda."

es.L: Y su padre y su madre le dijeron: «¿No hay mujer entre las hijas de tus hermanos, ni en todo mi pueblo, para que vayas tú a tomar mujer de los filisteos incircuncisos?». Y Sansón dijo a su padre: «A ella tómamela, porque ella es recta a mis ojos».
es.B: Su padre y su madre le dijeron: «¿No hay ninguna mujer entre tus parientes, ni en todo mi pueblo? ¿Tienes que ir a buscar esposa entre los filisteos incircuncisos?». Pero Sansón le dijo a su padre: «Consíguemela a ella. Es la que me parece bien a mí».
es.R: Su padre y su madre le dijeron: «¿No hay ninguna mujer entre nuestros parientes o en todo nuestro pueblo? ¿Por qué tienes que casarte con una filistea? ¡Ellos ni siquiera están circuncidados!». Pero Sansón le dijo a su padre: «Consíguemela. Es la que me gusta».

fr.L: Et son père et sa mère lui dirent : « N’y a-t-il pas de femme parmi les filles de tes frères et dans tout mon peuple, que tu ailles prendre une femme chez les Philistins, les incirconcis ? » Et Samson dit à son père : « Elle, prends-la-moi, car elle est droite à mes yeux. »
fr.B: Son père et sa mère lui dirent : « N’y a-t-il pas de femme parmi tes parents ou dans tout mon peuple ? Faut-il que tu ailles prendre une épouse chez ces incirconcis de Philistins ? » Mais Samson dit à son père : « Obtiens-la-moi. C’est elle qui me plaît. »
fr.R: Son père et sa mère lui ont dit : « N’y a-t-il pas de femme dans notre famille ou dans tout notre peuple ? Pourquoi faut-il que tu épouses une Philistine ? Ils ne sont même pas circoncis ! » Mais Samson a dit à son père : « Obtiens-la-moi. C’est elle que j’aime bien. »

vi.L: Cha mẹ ông nói với ông: "Trong các con gái của anh em con, hay trong cả dân của cha, không có người phụ nữ nào sao, mà con lại đi cưới vợ trong đám người Phi-li-tin không cắt bì?" Sam-sôn nói với cha mình: "Xin cha cưới nàng cho con, vì con thấy nàng là vừa mắt."
vi.B: Cha mẹ ông nói: "Trong bà con của con, hay trong cả dân của cha, không có người phụ nữ nào sao? Sao con lại phải đi cưới vợ trong đám người Phi-li-tin không cắt bì?" Nhưng Sam-sôn nói với cha: "Xin cha cưới cô ấy cho con. Con thấy cô ấy là người vừa ý con."
vi.R: Cha mẹ ông nói: "Trong bà con chúng ta, hay trong cả dân tộc chúng ta, không có người phụ nữ nào sao? Sao con lại phải đi cưới một người Phi-li-tin? Họ còn không chịu phép cắt bì nữa!" Nhưng Sam-sôn nói với cha: "Xin cha cưới cô ấy cho con. Con thích cô ấy."

ko.L: 그의 아버지와 어머니가 그에게 말했다. "네 형제들의 딸들 가운데나 내 모든 백성 가운데 여자가 없어서, 네가 할례 받지 않은 블레셋 사람들에게서 아내를 얻으려고 하느냐?" 삼손이 그의 아버지에게 말했다. "그 여자를 저에게 데려와 주십시오. 그 여자가 제 눈에 좋습니다."
ko.B: 그의 아버지와 어머니가 그에게 말했다. "네 친척들 가운데나 우리 백성 가운데에는 여자가 없느냐? 꼭 할례 받지 않은 블레셋 사람들에게 가서 아내를 얻어야 하겠느냐?" 그러나 삼손은 아버지에게 말했다. "그 여자를 저에게 데려와 주십시오. 저는 그 여자가 마음에 듭니다."
ko.R: 그의 아버지와 어머니가 그에게 말했다. "우리 친척들 가운데나 우리 백성 가운데 여자가 없느냐? 왜 꼭 블레셋 사람과 결혼하려고 하느냐? 그들은 할례도 받지 않은 사람들이다!" 그러나 삼손은 아버지에게 말했다. "그 여자를 데려와 주십시오. 저는 그 여자가 좋습니다."

decisions.choice: the uncircumcised Philistines: outsiders to Israel's covenant
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham's family (Genesis 17:10-14). The Philistines did not practice it, so "uncircumcised" marks them as outside that covenant; it is a term of contempt (1 Samuel 14:6; 17:26). Israel had been warned against marrying into the peoples around it (Exodus 34:16; Deuteronomy 7:3; Judges 3:6).

decisions.choice: she is right in my eyes: she pleases me
decisions.reason: The phrase means "she is the one I want". It is the phrase of the book's closing verdict, "each did what was right in his own eyes" (17:6; 21:25): Samson chooses by what he sees and likes, as verses 1 and 7 also show.

decisions.choice: my people: one parent speaks for both
decisions.reason: Both parents are named as speaking, but the text says "my people", not "our people". It is one voice speaking for the two of them; the sense is the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: Her take for me: "her" comes first
decisions.reason: Samson puts "her" at the front, against his parents' question: not some other woman, but this one.

decisions.choice: looks right to me / the one I like
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of seeing, which links this verse with 17:6 and 21:25; Readable says plainly that Samson likes her.

decisions.choice: our relatives, our people; They are not even circumcised!
decisions.reason: Readable uses "our" because both parents speak, and turns "the uncircumcised Philistines" into a short exclamation that carries the parents' dismay.

decisions.choice: "C'est elle qui me plaît" (B); "elle est droite à mes yeux" (L)
alternatives: "Elle me paraît bien", as the English "looks right to me"
decisions.reason: The English Balanced keeps the picture of the eyes ("looks right to me"). French "elle me plaît" says the same thing in natural words; Literal keeps the Hebrew "droite à mes yeux", the same words as "each did what was right in his own eyes" (17:6; 21:25), so the link stays visible there.

decisions.choice: "con thấy nàng là vừa mắt" at Literal for "she is right in my eyes"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "vừa mắt" keeps the eyes of the Hebrew idiom and its sense of being pleased by what one sees (meaning decision); Balanced says "vừa ý" and Readable "thích".

decisions.choice: "제 눈에 좋습니다" (is good in my eyes) at Literal; "마음에 듭니다" at Balanced
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "in my eyes", which the book repeats in 17:6 and 21:25; Balanced and Readable say it the way Korean does.

source.text: וְאָבִ֨יו וְאִמּ֜וֹ לֹ֣א יָדְע֗וּ כִּ֤י מֵיְהוָה֙ הִ֔יא כִּי־תֹאֲנָ֥ה הֽוּא־מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ מִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים מֹשְׁלִ֥ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And his father and his mother not knew that from Yahweh [was] it, for an occasion he [was] seeking from the Philistines. And at the time the that, [the] Philistines [were] ruling over Israel.

en.L: And his father and his mother did not know that it [was] from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [was] seeking an occasion against the Philistines. And at that time the Philistines [were] ruling over Israel.
en.B: His father and mother did not know that this came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was looking for an opportunity to act against the Philistines. At that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.
en.R: His father and mother did not know that this came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was looking for a reason to move against the Philistines, who were ruling over Israel at that time.

sw.L: Na baba yake na mama yake hawakujua ya kuwa jambo hilo [lilitoka] kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [alikuwa] akitafuta nafasi dhidi ya Wafilisti. Na wakati huo Wafilisti [walikuwa] wakiwatawala Israeli.
sw.B: Baba yake na mama yake hawakujua kwamba jambo hili lilitoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa akitafuta nafasi ya kuwashughulikia Wafilisti. Wakati huo Wafilisti walikuwa wakiwatawala Israeli.
sw.R: Baba yake na mama yake hawakujua kwamba jambo hili lilitoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa akitafuta sababu ya kuwashambulia Wafilisti, ambao wakati huo walikuwa wakiwatawala Israeli.

es.L: Y su padre y su madre no sabían que [esto venía] {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} buscaba una ocasión contra los filisteos. Y en aquel tiempo los filisteos dominaban sobre Israel.
es.B: Su padre y su madre no sabían que esto venía {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} buscaba una oportunidad para actuar contra los filisteos. En aquel tiempo los filisteos dominaban a Israel.
es.R: Su padre y su madre no sabían que esto venía {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} buscaba un motivo para actuar contra los filisteos, que en aquel tiempo dominaban a Israel.

fr.L: Et son père et sa mère ne savaient pas que cela [venait] {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} cherchait une occasion contre les Philistins. Et en ce temps-là, les Philistins dominaient sur Israël.
fr.B: Son père et sa mère ne savaient pas que cela venait {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} cherchait une occasion d’agir contre les Philistins. En ce temps-là, les Philistins dominaient sur Israël.
fr.R: Son père et sa mère ne savaient pas que cela venait {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} cherchait une raison d’agir contre les Philistins, qui dominaient Israël à cette époque.

vi.L: Cha mẹ ông không biết rằng việc ấy [là] từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang tìm dịp chống lại người Phi-li-tin. Lúc ấy người Phi-li-tin [đang] cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Cha mẹ ông không biết rằng việc này đến từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang tìm dịp để hành động chống lại người Phi-li-tin. Lúc ấy người Phi-li-tin đang cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Cha mẹ ông không biết rằng việc này đến từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang tìm cớ để ra tay chống lại người Phi-li-tin, là những người đang cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên lúc ấy.

ko.L: 그의 아버지와 어머니는 이 일이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 온 것인 줄을 알지 못했다. 그분께서 블레셋 사람들을 칠 기회를 찾고 계셨던 것이다. 그때에 블레셋 사람들이 이스라엘을 다스리고 있었다.
ko.B: 그의 아버지와 어머니는 이 일이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 온 것임을 알지 못했다. 그분께서는 블레셋 사람들을 치실 기회를 찾고 계셨다. 그때에는 블레셋 사람들이 이스라엘을 다스리고 있었다.
ko.R: 그의 아버지와 어머니는 이 일이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 일인 줄 몰랐다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 블레셋 사람들을 치실 이유를 찾고 계셨다. 그때에는 블레셋 사람들이 이스라엘을 다스리고 있었다.

decisions.choice: it was from the LORD: God was at work in Samson's choice
decisions.reason: The narrator tells the reader what the parents could not see: God was working through Samson's wish to marry a Philistine to bring about conflict with Israel's rulers. Scripture speaks the same way elsewhere of God working through human choices (Joshua 11:20; 1 Kings 12:15). This does not make the choice right; verse 3 has shown it was against what Israel was taught.

decisions.choice: he was seeking: the LORD
decisions.reason: "He" most naturally refers to the LORD, just named: God was seeking an occasion. It could also refer to Samson, looking for a reason to quarrel with the Philistines, but the sentence explains why the matter was "from the LORD", which fits God as the one seeking.

decisions.choice: an occasion: an opening, a pretext for a quarrel
decisions.reason: The noun occurs only here; a related verb is used in 2 Kings 5:7 of a king "seeking a quarrel". It is an occasion for conflict with the Philistines.

decisions.choice: the Philistines were ruling over Israel
decisions.reason: The Philistines had held Israel for forty years (13:1). There is no war in this story; Israel lives under them, which is why the conflict has to begin with one man.

decisions.choice: The LORD was looking
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD instead of "he", following the reading in m2.

source.text: וַיֵּ֧רֶד שִׁמְשׁ֛וֹן וְאָבִ֥יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ תִּמְנָ֑תָה וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ עַד־כַּרְמֵ֣י תִמְנָ֔תָה וְהִנֵּה֙ כְּפִ֣יר אֲרָי֔וֹת שֹׁאֵ֖ג לִקְרָאתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went down Samson and his father and his mother to Timnah, and they came to [the] vineyards of Timnah, and look, a young lion of lions roaring to meet him.

en.L: And Samson and his father and his mother went down to Timnah, and they came to the vineyards of Timnah, and look, a young lion of [the] lions [was] roaring to meet him.
en.B: Then Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. When they reached the vineyards of Timnah, a young lion suddenly came at him, roaring.
en.R: Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. Near the vineyards of Timnah, a young lion suddenly came roaring at Samson.

sw.L: Naye Samsoni akashuka pamoja na baba yake na mama yake mpaka Timna, wakafika kwenye mashamba ya mizabibu ya Timna, na tazama, mwana-simba [alikuwa] akinguruma kumkabili.
sw.B: Kisha Samsoni alishuka Timna pamoja na baba yake na mama yake. Walipofika kwenye mashamba ya mizabibu ya Timna, ghafla mwana-simba alimjia akinguruma.
sw.R: Samsoni alishuka Timna pamoja na baba yake na mama yake. Karibu na mashamba ya mizabibu ya Timna, ghafla mwana-simba alimjia Samsoni akinguruma.

es.L: Y descendió Sansón con su padre y su madre a Timnat, y llegaron a las viñas de Timnat, y he aquí un cachorro de león rugiendo a su encuentro.
es.B: Sansón descendió a Timnat con su padre y su madre. Cuando llegaron a las viñas de Timnat, de repente un león joven le salió al paso rugiendo.
es.R: Sansón bajó a Timnat con su padre y su madre. Cerca de las viñas de Timnat, de repente un león joven se lanzó rugiendo contra Sansón.

fr.L: Et Samson descendit, avec son père et sa mère, à Timna, et ils arrivèrent aux vignes de Timna, et voici, un jeune lion d’entre les lions rugissait à sa rencontre.
fr.B: Samson descendit donc à Timna avec son père et sa mère. Comme ils arrivaient aux vignes de Timna, un jeune lion surgit devant lui en rugissant.
fr.R: Samson est descendu à Timna avec son père et sa mère. Près des vignes de Timna, un jeune lion a tout à coup bondi vers Samson en rugissant.

vi.L: Sam-sôn cùng cha mẹ mình đi xuống Thim-na, và họ đến các vườn nho của Thim-na, và kìa, một con sư tử tơ gầm thét xông đến ông.
vi.B: Rồi Sam-sôn cùng cha mẹ đi xuống Thim-na. Khi họ đến các vườn nho của Thim-na, bỗng một con sư tử tơ gầm thét xông vào ông.
vi.R: Sam-sôn cùng cha mẹ đi xuống Thim-na. Gần các vườn nho của Thim-na, bỗng một con sư tử tơ gầm thét xông vào Sam-sôn.

ko.L: 삼손이 그의 아버지와 어머니와 함께 딤나로 내려가서 딤나의 포도원에 이르렀는데, 보라, 젊은 사자가 그를 향하여 으르렁거렸다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 삼손은 아버지와 어머니와 함께 딤나로 내려갔다. 그들이 딤나의 포도원에 이르렀을 때, 갑자기 젊은 사자 한 마리가 으르렁거리며 삼손에게 달려들었다.
ko.R: 삼손은 아버지와 어머니와 함께 딤나로 내려갔다. 딤나의 포도원 근처에서, 갑자기 젊은 사자 한 마리가 으르렁거리며 삼손에게 달려들었다.

decisions.choice: his parents went too, but the lion met Samson alone
decisions.reason: The parents travel with him, yet the lion comes "to meet him", and verse 6 says he did not tell them what happened. The text does not explain it; Samson must have been apart from them for a time, for example among the vineyards.

decisions.choice: a young lion of lions: a young lion in its full strength
decisions.reason: The word means a young lion that hunts for itself, past the cub stage and at its most dangerous (Ezekiel 19:2-3). "Of lions" stresses that it was a real lion.

decisions.choice: the vineyards of Timnah
decisions.reason: Samson was a Nazirite from birth (13:5, 7), and a Nazirite was to keep away from wine and from everything that comes from the vine (Numbers 6:3-4; Judges 13:14). The narrator places him among vineyards without comment.

decisions.choice: suddenly
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "look!" marks something sudden and unexpected; Balanced and Readable say "suddenly".

source.text: וַתִּצְלַ֨ח עָלָ֜יו ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֗ה וַֽיְשַׁסְּעֵ֨הוּ֙ כְּשַׁסַּ֣ע הַגְּדִ֔י וּמְא֖וּמָה אֵ֣ין בְּיָד֑וֹ וְלֹ֤א הִגִּיד֙ לְאָבִ֣יו וּלְאִמּ֔וֹ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: And rushed on him [the] Spirit of Yahweh, and he tore it as tearing the kid, and anything not [was] in his hand; and not he told his father and his mother what he had done.

en.L: And the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rushed on him, and he tore it apart as one tears apart a young goat, and there was nothing in his hand; and he did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.
en.B: The Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rushed on him, and with nothing in his hands he ripped the lion apart as easily as one rips apart a young goat. Yet he told neither his father nor his mother what he had done.
en.R: The Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rushed on Samson. He had no weapon, but he tore the lion apart as easily as tearing apart a little goat. He kept what he had done a secret from his father and mother.

sw.L: Naye Roho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjilia kwa nguvu, akampasua kama mtu apasuavyo mwana-mbuzi, wala hapakuwa na kitu mkononi mwake; lakini hakuwaambia baba yake wala mama yake alichokifanya.
sw.B: Roho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimjilia kwa nguvu, naye bila kitu chochote mikononi mwake akampasua yule simba kwa urahisi kama mtu apasuavyo mwana-mbuzi. Lakini hakumwambia baba yake wala mama yake alichokifanya.
sw.R: Roho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimjilia Samsoni kwa nguvu. Hakuwa na silaha, lakini alimpasua yule simba kwa urahisi kama mtu apasuavyo mwana-mbuzi mdogo. Aliweka siri alichokifanya, hakuwaambia baba yake na mama yake.

es.L: Y el Espíritu {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} irrumpió sobre él, y lo despedazó como se despedaza un cabrito, y nada había en su mano; y no contó a su padre ni a su madre lo que había hecho.
es.B: El Espíritu {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} irrumpió sobre él, y sin nada en las manos despedazó al león con la misma facilidad con que se despedaza un cabrito. Pero no les contó ni a su padre ni a su madre lo que había hecho.
es.R: El Espíritu {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino con fuerza sobre Sansón. Él no tenía ningún arma, pero despedazó al león tan fácilmente como si fuera un cabrito. No les dijo nada a su padre ni a su madre de lo que había hecho.

fr.L: Et l’Esprit {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fondit sur lui, et il le déchira comme on déchire un chevreau, et il n’avait rien dans sa main ; et il ne raconta pas à son père ni à sa mère ce qu’il avait fait.
fr.B: L’Esprit {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fondit sur lui, et sans rien dans les mains, il déchira le lion aussi facilement qu’on déchire un chevreau. Mais il ne raconta ni à son père ni à sa mère ce qu’il avait fait.
fr.R: L’Esprit {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est venu avec force sur Samson. Il n’avait pas d’arme, mais il a déchiré le lion aussi facilement qu’on déchire un petit chevreau. Il n’a rien dit à son père et à sa mère de ce qu’il avait fait.

vi.L: Thần Linh của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giáng mạnh trên ông, và ông xé nó ra như xé một con dê con, dù trong tay không có gì; nhưng ông không kể cho cha mẹ việc mình đã làm.
vi.B: Thần Linh của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giáng mạnh trên ông, và tay không, ông xé con sư tử ra dễ dàng như xé một con dê con. Nhưng ông không kể cho cha hay mẹ biết việc mình đã làm.
vi.R: Thần Linh của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giáng mạnh trên Sam-sôn. Ông không có vũ khí gì, nhưng ông xé con sư tử ra dễ dàng như xé một con dê nhỏ. Ông giữ kín việc mình đã làm, không cho cha mẹ biết.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 영이 그에게 세차게 임하시자, 그는 손에 아무것도 없이 염소 새끼를 찢듯이 그 사자를 찢었다. 그러나 그는 자기가 한 일을 아버지와 어머니에게 알리지 않았다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 영이 그에게 세차게 임하시자, 그는 맨손으로 염소 새끼를 찢듯이 쉽게 그 사자를 찢어 버렸다. 그러나 그는 자기가 한 일을 아버지에게도 어머니에게도 말하지 않았다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 영이 갑자기 삼손에게 강하게 임하셨다. 그는 손에 무기가 없었지만, 어린 염소를 찢듯이 쉽게 사자를 찢어 죽였다. 그러나 그는 자기가 한 일을 아버지와 어머니에게 말하지 않았다.

decisions.choice: rushed on him: came on him suddenly and with force
decisions.reason: The verb means to rush or break through. It is used of the Spirit coming on Samson again in 14:19 and 15:14, and on Saul and David (1 Samuel 10:6, 10; 11:6; 16:13). It is stronger than "was on him" (3:10; 11:29).

decisions.choice: the Spirit of the LORD: God's power giving strength
decisions.reason: As with the other judges (3:10; 6:34; 11:29), the Spirit of the LORD gives strength beyond the ordinary. In Samson's case it shows as bodily strength; his strength is God's gift, not his own (13:25; 16:20).

decisions.choice: as one tears a young goat: with ease
decisions.reason: A young goat is a small animal; the comparison shows how little effort it took Samson to tear apart a lion. "Nothing in his hand" means he had no weapon.

decisions.choice: he did not tell his father or his mother
decisions.reason: His silence is what makes the riddle impossible to guess (verses 9, 14, 16).

decisions.choice: as easily as
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the point of the comparison (m3).

decisions.choice: with nothing in his hands / He had no weapon
decisions.reason: "Nothing in his hand" is put in common English.

decisions.choice: "alimjilia kwa nguvu" (came on him with force) for the Spirit rushing on Samson
decisions.reason: The verb here is stronger than "was on" in 11:29: the Spirit comes suddenly and with force (m1). "Kumjilia kwa nguvu" keeps the agreed "kumjia" and adds the force, so the reader still hears the same Spirit of the LORD.

decisions.choice: "irrumpió sobre él" (L, B); "vino con fuerza sobre" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb here is not the plain "came on" of 11:29 but one that means coming suddenly and with force (m1). "Irrumpir" says that; Readable says it in simpler words.

decisions.choice: "fondit sur lui" (L, B); "est venu avec force sur" (R)
decisions.reason: A stronger verb than in 11:29 and 13:25: the Spirit comes on Samson suddenly and with force (m1). "Fondre sur" says that in French; Readable says it in plain words. The same wording is used in 14:19 and 15:14.

decisions.choice: "giáng mạnh trên" for "rushed on"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is stronger than the usual "came on" (meaning decision), so the Vietnamese uses a stronger verb than the "ngự trên" of the terms note, here and wherever the Spirit "rushes" on Samson.

decisions.choice: "세차게 임하다" (came on him with force)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb here is stronger than the usual "came on"; Korean adds "세차게" or "강하게" to the set phrase "주의 영이 임하였다" so that both the link and the force show.

source.text: וַיֵּ֖רֶד וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר לָאִשָּׁ֑ה וַתִּישַׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י שִׁמְשֽׁוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in [the] eyes of Samson.

en.L: And he went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in the eyes of Samson.
en.B: Then he went down and talked with the woman, and she looked right to Samson.
en.R: Then Samson went on down and talked with the woman. He liked her.

sw.L: Naye akashuka, akasema na yule mwanamke, naye alikuwa sawa machoni pa Samsoni.
sw.B: Kisha alishuka, akazungumza na yule mwanamke, naye akamfaa Samsoni machoni pake.
sw.R: Kisha Samsoni aliendelea kushuka, akazungumza na yule mwanamke. Alimpenda.

es.L: Y descendió y habló con la mujer, y ella fue recta a los ojos de Sansón.
es.B: Luego descendió y habló con la mujer, y a Sansón le pareció bien.
es.R: Después Sansón siguió bajando y habló con la mujer. Ella le gustó.

fr.L: Et il descendit et parla à la femme, et elle fut droite aux yeux de Samson.
fr.B: Puis il descendit parler avec la femme, et elle plut à Samson.
fr.R: Ensuite Samson est descendu parler avec la femme. Elle lui plaisait.

vi.L: Ông đi xuống và nói chuyện với người phụ nữ, và Sam-sôn thấy nàng là vừa mắt.
vi.B: Rồi ông đi xuống nói chuyện với người phụ nữ, và Sam-sôn thấy cô ấy vừa ý mình.
vi.R: Rồi Sam-sôn đi xuống nói chuyện với người phụ nữ. Ông thích cô ấy.

ko.L: 그가 내려가서 그 여자와 이야기하였는데, 그 여자가 삼손의 눈에 좋았다.
ko.B: 그러고 나서 그는 내려가서 그 여자와 이야기를 나누었고, 삼손은 그 여자가 마음에 들었다.
ko.R: 그러고 나서 삼손은 내려가서 그 여자와 이야기를 나누었다. 삼손은 그 여자가 좋았다.

decisions.choice: she was right in Samson's eyes: he was pleased with her
decisions.reason: The same phrase as in verse 3 (see the note there), now said by the narrator: having talked with her, Samson is pleased with his choice.

decisions.choice: spoke to the woman
decisions.reason: Samson now speaks with her himself; in verses 1-3 he had only seen her. The marriage agreement itself is made by his father (verse 10).

decisions.choice: looked right to / He liked her
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

source.text: וַיָּ֤שָׁב מִיָּמִים֙ לְקַחְתָּ֔הּ וַיָּ֣סַר לִרְא֔וֹת אֵ֖ת מַפֶּ֣לֶת הָאַרְיֵ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה עֲדַ֧ת דְּבוֹרִ֛ים בִּגְוִיַּ֥ת הָאַרְיֵ֖ה וּדְבָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he returned after days to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and look, a swarm of bees [was] in [the] body of the lion, and honey.

en.L: And he returned after [some] days to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and look, a swarm of bees [was] in the body of the lion, and honey.
en.B: Some time later he went back to marry her, and he turned aside to look at the lion's carcass. There in the lion's body was a swarm of bees, and honey.
en.R: Some time later Samson went back to marry her. On the way he left the road to look at the dead lion. Inside the lion's body he found a swarm of bees and some honey.

sw.L: Naye akarudi baada ya siku [kadhaa] kumtwaa, akageuka kando kuuona mzoga wa yule simba, na tazama, kundi la nyuki [lilikuwa] ndani ya mwili wa simba, na asali.
sw.B: Baada ya muda alirudi kumwoa, akageuka kando kuutazama mzoga wa yule simba. Humo ndani ya mwili wa simba kulikuwa na kundi la nyuki, na asali.
sw.R: Baada ya muda Samsoni alirudi kumwoa. Njiani aliiacha njia kwenda kumtazama yule simba aliyekufa. Ndani ya mwili wa simba alikuta kundi la nyuki na asali.

es.L: Y volvió después de [algunos] días para tomarla, y se apartó para ver el cadáver del león, y he aquí un enjambre de abejas [había] en el cuerpo del león, y miel.
es.B: Algún tiempo después volvió para casarse con ella, y se desvió para ver el cadáver del león. Dentro del cuerpo del león había un enjambre de abejas, y miel.
es.R: Algún tiempo después, Sansón volvió para casarse con ella. En el camino se apartó para ver el león muerto. Dentro del cuerpo del león encontró un enjambre de abejas y un poco de miel.

fr.L: Et il revint après [quelque] temps pour la prendre, et il se détourna pour voir le cadavre du lion, et voici, un essaim d’abeilles [était] dans le corps du lion, et du miel.
fr.B: Quelque temps après, il revint pour l’épouser, et il fit un détour pour voir le cadavre du lion. Il y avait dans le corps du lion un essaim d’abeilles, et du miel.
fr.R: Quelque temps plus tard, Samson est retourné à Timna pour l’épouser. En chemin, il a quitté la route pour aller voir le lion mort. Dans le corps du lion, il a trouvé un essaim d’abeilles et du miel.

vi.L: Sau [một thời gian], ông trở lại để cưới nàng, và ông rẽ vào xem xác con sư tử, và kìa, có một đàn ong trong xác sư tử, và có mật.
vi.B: Một thời gian sau, ông trở lại để cưới cô ấy, và ông rẽ vào xem xác con sư tử. Trong xác sư tử có một đàn ong và mật ong.
vi.R: Một thời gian sau, Sam-sôn trở lại để cưới cô ấy. Dọc đường ông rẽ khỏi lối đi để xem con sư tử chết. Ông thấy trong xác nó có một đàn ong và một ít mật.

ko.L: 얼마 뒤에 그가 그 여자를 맞으러 돌아가다가, 그 사자의 주검을 보려고 길을 벗어났는데, 보라, 그 사자의 몸 안에 벌 떼와 꿀이 있었다.
ko.B: 얼마 뒤에 그는 그 여자와 결혼하려고 다시 내려가다가, 사자의 주검을 보려고 길을 벗어났다. 그런데 그 사자의 몸 안에 벌 떼가 있었고, 꿀도 있었다.
ko.R: 얼마 뒤에 삼손은 그 여자와 결혼하려고 다시 갔다. 가는 길에 그는 죽은 사자를 보려고 길에서 벗어났다. 사자의 몸 안에는 벌 떼가 있었고, 꿀도 있었다.

decisions.choice: after days: some time later
decisions.reason: "After days" is an unspecified time. The same word "days" can stand for a year (1 Samuel 1:21; Judges 11:40), and enough time had passed for the carcass to dry out and for bees to make honey, but the text gives no exact length.

decisions.choice: to take her: to marry her
decisions.reason: "Take" a woman is the usual way of saying "marry" (verse 2).

decisions.choice: a swarm of bees and honey in the carcass
decisions.reason: Wild bees make their nests in hollow places. By now the carcass had dried in the heat, and a swarm had settled in it and made honey. The word for "carcass" means "what has fallen"; the second word, "body", is used of a dead body (1 Samuel 31:10).

decisions.choice: On the way he left the road
decisions.reason: "Turned aside" means he went off his route; Readable says so.

source.text: וַיִּרְדֵּ֣הוּ אֶל־כַּפָּ֗יו וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וְאָכֹ֔ל וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל־אָבִ֣יו וְאֶל־אִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם וַיֹּאכֵ֑לוּ וְלֹֽא־הִגִּ֣יד לָהֶ֔ם כִּ֛י מִגְּוִיַּ֥ת הָאַרְיֵ֖ה רָדָ֥ה הַדְּבָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he scraped it into his palms, and he went, going and eating, and he went to his father and to his mother, and he gave to them, and they ate; and not he told them that from [the] body of the lion he had scraped the honey.

en.L: And he scraped it into his palms and went on, going and eating, and he came to his father and to his mother and gave [some] to them, and they ate; but he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey out of the body of the lion.
en.B: He scooped the honey out into his hands and went on, eating as he walked. When he reached his father and mother, he gave them some, and they ate. Yet he did not tell them he had scooped the honey out of the lion's carcass.
en.R: He scooped some honey into his hands and walked on, eating it. When he got back to his father and mother, he gave them some, and they ate it too. But he did not say that the honey came from the dead lion's body.

sw.L: Naye akaikomba kwa viganja vyake, akaenda, akienda na kula, akafika kwa baba yake na mama yake, akawapa, nao wakala; lakini hakuwaambia ya kuwa ameikomba asali hiyo kutoka mwilini mwa yule simba.
sw.B: Aliikomba asali kwa mikono yake, akaendelea na safari, akila huku akitembea. Alipowafikia baba yake na mama yake, aliwapa nao wakala. Lakini hakuwaambia kwamba aliikomba asali hiyo kutoka katika mzoga wa yule simba.
sw.R: Alikomba asali kidogo kwa mikono yake, akaendelea kutembea akiila. Aliporudi kwa baba yake na mama yake, aliwapa, nao wakala pia. Lakini hakusema kwamba asali hiyo ilitoka katika mwili wa simba aliyekufa.

es.L: Y la sacó en sus palmas y siguió andando y comiendo, y llegó a su padre y a su madre y les dio, y comieron; pero no les contó que había sacado la miel del cuerpo del león.
es.B: Sacó la miel con las manos y siguió su camino, comiendo mientras andaba. Cuando llegó adonde estaban su padre y su madre, les dio, y comieron. Pero no les dijo que había sacado la miel del cadáver del león.
es.R: Sacó un poco de miel con las manos y siguió caminando mientras comía. Cuando volvió adonde estaban su padre y su madre, les dio un poco, y ellos también comieron. Pero no les dijo que la miel venía del cuerpo del león muerto.

fr.L: Et il le racla dans ses paumes et s’en alla, marchant et mangeant, et il alla vers son père et vers sa mère et leur en donna, et ils mangèrent ; mais il ne leur raconta pas qu’il avait raclé le miel du corps du lion.
fr.B: Il recueillit le miel dans ses mains et poursuivit sa route en mangeant. Quand il eut rejoint son père et sa mère, il leur en donna, et ils en mangèrent. Mais il ne leur dit pas qu’il avait pris ce miel dans le cadavre du lion.
fr.R: Il a pris du miel dans ses mains et il a continué son chemin en le mangeant. Quand il est arrivé chez son père et sa mère, il leur en a donné, et ils en ont mangé eux aussi. Mais il ne leur a pas dit que le miel venait du corps du lion mort.

vi.L: Ông vét mật vào lòng bàn tay và đi tiếp, vừa đi vừa ăn, rồi ông đến với cha mẹ mình và cho họ [một ít], và họ ăn; nhưng ông không cho họ biết rằng ông đã vét mật ấy từ xác sư tử.
vi.B: Ông vét mật vào tay và đi tiếp, vừa đi vừa ăn. Khi về đến chỗ cha mẹ, ông cho họ một ít, và họ cũng ăn. Nhưng ông không cho họ biết rằng ông đã vét mật ấy từ xác sư tử.
vi.R: Ông vét một ít mật vào tay và vừa đi vừa ăn. Khi về đến chỗ cha mẹ, ông cho họ một ít, và họ cũng ăn. Nhưng ông không nói rằng mật ấy lấy từ xác con sư tử chết.

ko.L: 그는 그 꿀을 손바닥에 긁어 담고 걸어가면서 먹었다. 그리고 아버지와 어머니에게 가서 [얼마를] 그들에게 주었고, 그들도 먹었다. 그러나 그는 그 꿀을 사자의 몸에서 긁어낸 것을 그들에게 알리지 않았다.
ko.B: 그는 꿀을 손으로 떠내어 걸어가면서 먹었다. 아버지와 어머니에게 이르자 그들에게도 조금 주었고, 그들도 먹었다. 그러나 그는 그 꿀을 사자의 주검에서 떠낸 것이라고 말하지 않았다.
ko.R: 삼손은 꿀을 손으로 떠서 걸어가면서 먹었다. 아버지와 어머니에게 돌아와서 그들에게도 조금 주었고, 그들도 먹었다. 그러나 그는 그 꿀이 죽은 사자의 몸에서 나온 것이라고 말하지 않았다.

decisions.choice: scraped: scooped out
decisions.reason: The verb, used here twice, means to scrape or scoop something out. Samson takes the comb out with his hands.

decisions.choice: honey from a carcass
decisions.reason: Touching a dead animal made a person unclean (Leviticus 11:24-25, 39), and a Nazirite was to keep away from the dead (Numbers 6:6). The narrator makes no comment, but his silence before his parents, who also eat, suggests Samson knew they would object.

decisions.choice: he did not tell them
decisions.reason: The second time the narrator says this (verse 6). No one but Samson knows where the honey came from, which is the secret of the riddle in verse 14.

decisions.choice: scooped ... into his hands
decisions.reason: "Palms" in the Hebrew; "hands" is the common English word.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥רֶד אָבִ֖יהוּ אֶל־הָאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיַּ֨עַשׂ שָׁ֤ם שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן יַעֲשׂ֖וּ הַבַּחוּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And went down his father to the woman, and made there Samson a feast, for so used to do the young men.

en.L: And his father went down to the woman, and Samson made a feast there, for so the young men used to do.
en.B: His father went down to see the woman, and Samson held a feast there, as young men used to do.
en.R: Then his father went down to Timnah to see the woman's family. Samson gave a wedding feast there, because that was the custom for young men when they married.

sw.L: Naye baba yake akashuka kwa yule mwanamke, naye Samsoni akafanya karamu huko, kwa maana ndivyo walivyokuwa wakifanya vijana.
sw.B: Baba yake alishuka kumwona yule mwanamke, naye Samsoni akafanya karamu huko, kama vijana walivyokuwa wakifanya.
sw.R: Kisha baba yake alishuka Timna kuionana na jamaa ya yule mwanamke. Samsoni alifanya karamu ya harusi huko, kwa sababu hiyo ndiyo ilikuwa desturi ya vijana walipooa.

es.L: Y descendió su padre a la mujer, e hizo allí Sansón un banquete, porque así solían hacer los jóvenes.
es.B: Su padre descendió a ver a la mujer, y Sansón dio allí un banquete, como solían hacer los jóvenes.
es.R: Después su padre bajó a Timnat para ver a la familia de la mujer. Sansón dio allí un banquete de bodas, porque esa era la costumbre de los jóvenes cuando se casaban.

fr.L: Et son père descendit vers la femme, et Samson fit là un festin, car ainsi faisaient les jeunes gens.
fr.B: Son père descendit voir la femme, et Samson donna là un festin, comme les jeunes gens avaient coutume de le faire.
fr.R: Ensuite, son père est descendu à Timna pour voir la famille de la femme. Samson a donné là-bas un festin de noces, parce que c’était la coutume pour les jeunes hommes quand ils se mariaient.

vi.L: Cha ông đi xuống đến người phụ nữ, và Sam-sôn đãi tiệc tại đó, vì các chàng trai thường làm như vậy.
vi.B: Cha ông đi xuống gặp người phụ nữ, và Sam-sôn đãi tiệc tại đó, như các chàng trai thường làm.
vi.R: Rồi cha ông đi xuống Thim-na gặp gia đình người phụ nữ. Sam-sôn đãi tiệc cưới tại đó, vì đó là phong tục của các chàng trai khi cưới vợ.

ko.L: 그의 아버지가 그 여자에게 내려갔고, 삼손은 거기에서 잔치를 베풀었다. 젊은이들은 그렇게 하는 것이 관습이었다.
ko.B: 그의 아버지가 그 여자를 만나러 내려갔고, 삼손은 거기에서 잔치를 베풀었다. 그 무렵 젊은이들은 그렇게 하곤 했다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 삼손의 아버지는 그 여자의 집안을 만나러 딤나로 내려갔다. 삼손은 거기에서 혼인 잔치를 베풀었다. 그때에는 젊은이가 결혼할 때 그렇게 하는 것이 관습이었다.

decisions.choice: a feast: a wedding feast with drinking
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "drink" and names a feast where wine was served. Here it is the wedding feast, which lasted seven days (verse 12; Genesis 29:22, 27). The narrator does not say whether Samson drank, but a Nazirite was to drink no wine (13:4, 7, 14; Numbers 6:3).

decisions.choice: so the young men used to do: the bridegroom's custom
decisions.reason: The narrator explains a custom of an earlier time: the bridegroom gave the feast. The words show the story is told to readers for whom that custom was no longer familiar.

decisions.choice: his father went down
decisions.reason: The father goes to settle the marriage with the woman's family, as Samson asked in verses 2-3.

decisions.choice: to see the woman / to see the woman's family
decisions.reason: "Went down to the woman" means he went to her home to complete the arrangements. Balanced adds "to see"; Readable says it was her family he went to meet.

source.text: וַיְהִ֖י כִּרְאוֹתָ֣ם אוֹת֑וֹ וַיִּקְחוּ֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים מֵֽרֵעִ֔ים וַיִּהְי֖וּ אִתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when they saw him, and they took thirty companions, and they were with him.

en.L: And it happened, when they saw him, that they took thirty companions, and they were with him.
en.B: When the people there saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.
en.R: When the Philistines there saw Samson, they chose thirty young men to keep him company.

sw.L: Ikawa walipomwona, wakatwaa wenzi thelathini, nao wakawa pamoja naye.
sw.B: Watu wa huko walipomwona, walileta wenzi thelathini wakae pamoja naye.
sw.R: Wafilisti wa huko walipomwona Samsoni, walichagua vijana thelathini wakae pamoja naye.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando lo vieron, tomaron treinta compañeros, y estuvieron con él.
es.B: Cuando la gente de allí lo vio, le dieron treinta compañeros para que estuvieran con él.
es.R: Cuando los filisteos de allí vieron a Sansón, escogieron a treinta jóvenes para que lo acompañaran.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand ils le virent, qu’ils prirent trente compagnons, et ils furent avec lui.
fr.B: Quand les gens du lieu le virent, ils amenèrent trente compagnons pour être avec lui.
fr.R: Quand les Philistins de la ville ont vu Samson, ils ont choisi trente jeunes hommes pour lui tenir compagnie.

vi.L: Khi họ thấy ông, họ đem đến ba mươi người bạn, và những người ấy ở với ông.
vi.B: Khi dân ở đó thấy ông, họ đem đến ba mươi người bạn để ở với ông.
vi.R: Khi người Phi-li-tin ở đó thấy Sam-sôn, họ chọn ba mươi chàng trai đến ở cùng ông.

ko.L: 그들이 그를 보았을 때에, 친구 서른 명을 데려와 그와 함께 있게 하였다.
ko.B: 그곳 사람들은 삼손을 보고, 친구 서른 명을 데려와 그와 함께 있게 하였다.
ko.R: 그곳 블레셋 사람들은 삼손을 보고, 젊은이 서른 명을 뽑아 그와 함께 있게 하였다.

decisions.choice: when they saw him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "saw". The ancient Greek translation reads "when they feared him", which in Hebrew is a very similar-looking verb. The Hebrew makes good sense and is followed here; the Greek may reflect the idea that the thirty were also there to watch a dangerous man.

decisions.choice: thirty companions: the bridegroom's attendants
decisions.reason: The bride's town provided young men as the bridegroom's companions at the feast. Their number matters for the wager in verses 12-13 and for the thirty men of verse 19. One of them was his chief friend (verse 20).

decisions.choice: they: the people of Timnah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name who chose the companions; it is the bride's people, "the men of the city" of verse 18.

decisions.choice: the people there / the Philistines there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the unstated subject (m3).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אָחֽוּדָה־נָּ֥א לָכֶ֖ם חִידָ֑ה אִם־הַגֵּ֣ד תַּגִּידוּ֩ אוֹתָ֨הּ לִ֜י שִׁבְעַ֨ת יְמֵ֤י הַמִּשְׁתֶּה֙ וּמְצָאתֶ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָכֶם֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים סְדִינִ֔ים וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים חֲלִפֹ֥ת בְּגָדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Samson, let me riddle please to you a riddle; if telling you tell it to me [in] the seven days of the feast and find [it] out, and I will give to you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of garments.

en.L: And Samson said to them, "Let me pose a riddle to you. If you can really tell it to me in the seven days of the feast and find [it] out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.
en.B: Samson said to them, "Let me give you a riddle. If you can explain it to me during the seven days of the feast and work it out, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of festive clothes.
en.R: Samson said to them, "Let me ask you a riddle. The feast lasts seven days. If you can give me the answer before it is over, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of fine clothes.

sw.L: Naye Samsoni akawaambia, "Niwategee kitendawili. Kama kweli mtaweza kuniambia jibu lake katika zile siku saba za karamu na kukitegua, basi nitawapa mavazi thelathini ya kitani na nguo thelathini za kubadilisha.
sw.B: Samsoni aliwaambia, "Niwategee kitendawili. Kama mtaweza kunieleza jibu lake katika siku saba za karamu na kukitegua, nitawapa mavazi thelathini ya kitani na mavazi thelathini ya sikukuu.
sw.R: Samsoni aliwaambia, "Niwategee kitendawili. Karamu inachukua siku saba. Kama mtaweza kunipa jibu kabla haijaisha, nitawapa mavazi thelathini ya kitani na mavazi thelathini mazuri.

es.L: Y Sansón les dijo: «{{plural_you:Permítanme proponerles|Permitidme proponeros}} un enigma. Si de veras me lo {{plural_you:declaran|declaráis}} en los siete días del banquete y lo {{plural_you:descubren|descubrís}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} daré treinta túnicas de lino y treinta mudas de ropa.
es.B: Sansón les dijo: «Voy a {{plural_you:proponerles|proponeros}} una adivinanza. Si me la {{plural_you:explican|explicáis}} y la {{plural_you:resuelven|resolvéis}} durante los siete días del banquete, {{plural_you:les|os}} daré treinta túnicas de lino y treinta mudas de ropa de fiesta.
es.R: Sansón les dijo: «Voy a {{plural_you:hacerles|haceros}} una adivinanza. El banquete dura siete días. Si me {{plural_you:dan|dais}} la respuesta antes de que termine, {{plural_you:les|os}} daré treinta túnicas de lino y treinta mudas de ropa fina.

fr.L: Et Samson leur dit : « Laissez-moi donc vous proposer une énigme. Si vraiment vous me l’expliquez pendant les sept jours du festin et que vous [la] découvrez, je vous donnerai trente tuniques de lin et trente vêtements de rechange.
fr.B: Samson leur dit : « Je vais vous proposer une énigme. Si vous pouvez me l’expliquer pendant les sept jours du festin et la résoudre, je vous donnerai trente tuniques de lin et trente habits de fête.
fr.R: Samson leur a dit : « Je vais vous poser une devinette. Le festin dure sept jours. Si vous pouvez me donner la réponse avant la fin, je vous donnerai trente tuniques de lin et trente beaux habits.

vi.L: Sam-sôn nói với họ: "Tôi xin ra cho các anh một câu đố. Nếu trong bảy ngày tiệc các anh thật sự giải được và tìm ra [lời đáp], thì tôi sẽ cho các anh ba mươi áo vải gai mịn và ba mươi bộ áo lễ.
vi.B: Sam-sôn nói với họ: "Tôi ra cho các anh một câu đố. Nếu trong bảy ngày tiệc các anh giải được và tìm ra lời đáp, tôi sẽ cho các anh ba mươi áo vải gai mịn và ba mươi bộ áo lễ.
vi.R: Sam-sôn nói với họ: "Tôi đố các anh một câu. Tiệc kéo dài bảy ngày. Nếu các anh trả lời được trước khi tiệc tàn, tôi sẽ cho các anh ba mươi áo vải gai mịn và ba mươi bộ áo đẹp.

ko.L: 삼손이 그들에게 말했다. "내가 너희에게 수수께끼를 하나 내겠다. 너희가 잔치하는 이레 동안에 그것을 풀어 나에게 말하면, 내가 너희에게 고운 베옷 서른 벌과 갈아입을 옷 서른 벌을 주겠다.
ko.B: 삼손이 그들에게 말했다. "내가 너희에게 수수께끼를 하나 내겠다. 잔치가 열리는 이레 동안 너희가 그 답을 알아내어 나에게 말하면, 내가 너희에게 고운 베옷 서른 벌과 잔치 때 입는 옷 서른 벌을 주겠다.
ko.R: 삼손이 그들에게 말했다. "내가 너희에게 수수께끼를 하나 내겠다. 잔치는 이레 동안 계속된다. 잔치가 끝나기 전에 너희가 답을 맞히면, 내가 너희에게 고운 베옷 서른 벌과 좋은 옷 서른 벌을 주겠다.

decisions.choice: a riddle: a puzzling saying to be solved
decisions.reason: Verb and noun come from the same root: literally "let me riddle you a riddle". The word can name any dark or puzzling saying (Numbers 12:8; 1 Kings 10:1; Psalm 49:5); here it is a riddle posed as a wager.

decisions.choice: if you can really tell it
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: "if you indeed tell it". "Tell" a riddle means give its answer; "find it out" means solve it.

decisions.choice: linen garments: costly linen clothing
decisions.reason: The word names a fine linen garment, a mark of wealth (Proverbs 31:24; Isaiah 3:23). Its exact shape is not known.

decisions.choice: changes of clothes: fine clothing for special occasions
decisions.reason: "Changes" are sets of clothing worn in place of everyday clothes, given as rich gifts (Genesis 45:22; 2 Kings 5:5, 22-23). The prize is large: a full outfit for each of the thirty.

decisions.choice: pose a riddle
decisions.reason: English has no verb "to riddle" in this sense, so Literal uses "pose a riddle" and the note gives the Hebrew pattern.

decisions.choice: sets of festive clothes / sets of fine clothes
decisions.reason: "Changes of garments" means good clothes to change into; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: "kitendawili" for the riddle, with "kutega" (to pose) and "kutegua" (to solve)
decisions.reason: "Kitendawili" is the Swahili riddle, a puzzling saying put to others to be solved, and Swahili has its own verbs for setting and solving one; "fumbo" is a mystery or puzzle in general.

decisions.choice: "enigma" (L); "adivinanza" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew pairing of verb and noun ("riddle a riddle") with "proponer un enigma"; Balanced and Readable use "adivinanza", the everyday Spanish word for a puzzle to be solved (m1).

decisions.choice: "une énigme" (L, B); "une devinette" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names a puzzling saying to be solved (m1). "Énigme" is the usual French word; Readable uses "devinette", the everyday word a young reader knows for a riddle with an answer.

decisions.choice: Samson and the thirty companions say "tôi" and "các anh" / "anh"
decisions.reason: Young men of about the same age who are not kin; the polite but familiar "anh" fits wedding companions.

decisions.choice: Samson and his thirty Philistine companions speak to each other in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: They are young men of the same age at a wedding feast, and the talk turns quickly to threats; the plain style fits both.

source.text: וְאִם־לֹ֣א תוּכְלוּ֮ לְהַגִּ֣יד לִי֒ וּנְתַתֶּ֨ם אַתֶּ֥ם לִי֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים סְדִינִ֔ים וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים חֲלִיפ֣וֹת בְּגָדִ֑ים וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ ח֥וּדָה חִידָתְךָ֖ וְנִשְׁמָעֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And if not you are able to tell me, and you will give, you, to me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of garments. And they said to him, riddle your riddle, and we will hear it.

en.L: But if you are not able to tell me, then you will give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes." And they said to him, "Pose your riddle, and let us hear it."
en.B: But if you cannot tell me, then you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of festive clothes." They said to him, "Tell us your riddle. Let us hear it."
en.R: But if you cannot tell me the answer, then you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of fine clothes." They answered, "Ask your riddle. Let us hear it."

sw.L: Lakini kama hamtaweza kuniambia, basi ninyi mtanipa mimi mavazi thelathini ya kitani na nguo thelathini za kubadilisha." Nao wakamwambia, "Tega kitendawili chako, tukisikie."
sw.B: Lakini kama hamtaweza kunieleza, basi ninyi lazima mnipe mavazi thelathini ya kitani na mavazi thelathini ya sikukuu." Wakamwambia, "Tutegee kitendawili chako. Tukisikie."
sw.R: Lakini kama hamtaweza kunipa jibu, basi lazima mnipe mavazi thelathini ya kitani na mavazi thelathini mazuri." Walijibu, "Tega kitendawili chako. Tukisikie."

es.L: Pero si no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} declarármelo, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:darán|daréis}} treinta túnicas de lino y treinta mudas de ropa». Y ellos le dijeron: «Propón tu enigma, y lo oiremos».
es.B: Pero si no me la {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} explicar, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:darán|daréis}} a mí treinta túnicas de lino y treinta mudas de ropa de fiesta». Ellos le dijeron: «Dinos tu adivinanza. Vamos a oírla».
es.R: Pero si no me {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} dar la respuesta, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:darán|daréis}} treinta túnicas de lino y treinta mudas de ropa fina». Ellos le respondieron: «Haznos tu adivinanza. Vamos a oírla».

fr.L: Mais si vous ne pouvez pas me l’expliquer, vous, vous me donnerez trente tuniques de lin et trente vêtements de rechange. » Et ils lui dirent : « Propose ton énigme, et nous l’écouterons. »
fr.B: Mais si vous ne pouvez pas me l’expliquer, c’est vous qui me donnerez trente tuniques de lin et trente habits de fête. » Ils lui dirent : « Propose-nous ton énigme. Écoutons-la. »
fr.R: Mais si vous ne pouvez pas me donner la réponse, c’est vous qui devrez me donner trente tuniques de lin et trente beaux habits. » Ils lui ont répondu : « Pose ta devinette. Nous t’écoutons. »

vi.L: Nhưng nếu các anh không giải được, thì chính các anh phải cho tôi ba mươi áo vải gai mịn và ba mươi bộ áo lễ." Họ nói với ông: "Anh hãy ra câu đố đi, để chúng tôi nghe."
vi.B: Nhưng nếu các anh không giải được, thì các anh phải cho tôi ba mươi áo vải gai mịn và ba mươi bộ áo lễ." Họ nói với ông: "Anh ra câu đố đi. Chúng tôi nghe đây."
vi.R: Nhưng nếu các anh không trả lời được, thì các anh phải cho tôi ba mươi áo vải gai mịn và ba mươi bộ áo đẹp." Họ trả lời: "Anh đố đi. Chúng tôi nghe đây."

ko.L: 그러나 너희가 나에게 말하지 못하면, 너희가 나에게 고운 베옷 서른 벌과 갈아입을 옷 서른 벌을 주어야 한다." 그들이 그에게 말했다. "네 수수께끼를 내 보아라. 우리가 들어 보자."
ko.B: 그러나 너희가 답을 말하지 못하면, 너희가 나에게 고운 베옷 서른 벌과 잔치 때 입는 옷 서른 벌을 주어야 한다." 그들이 그에게 말했다. "네 수수께끼를 말해 보아라. 들어 보자."
ko.R: 그러나 너희가 답을 말하지 못하면, 너희가 나에게 고운 베옷 서른 벌과 좋은 옷 서른 벌을 주어야 한다." 그들이 대답했다. "수수께끼를 내 보아라. 들어 보자."

decisions.choice: you will give: "you" stressed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the pronoun "you" to the verb: the wager runs both ways. Samson stands alone against thirty, so if he wins, he gains thirty sets of clothing at once.

decisions.choice: pose your riddle, and let us hear it: a ready acceptance
decisions.reason: The companions accept the wager at once. The verb and noun are again from the same root, as in verse 12.

decisions.choice: Tell us your riddle / Ask your riddle
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם מֵהָֽאֹכֵל֙ יָצָ֣א מַאֲכָ֔ל וּמֵעַ֖ז יָצָ֣א מָת֑וֹק וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֛וּ לְהַגִּ֥יד הַחִידָ֖ה שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, from the eater came out food, and from [the] strong came out sweet; and not they were able to tell the riddle three days.

en.L: And he said to them, \q "From the eater came out food, \q and from [the] strong came out [something] sweet." \q And they were not able to tell the riddle [for] three days.
en.B: He said to them, \q "From the one who eats came food; \q from the strong one came something sweet." \q For three days they could not explain the riddle.
en.R: So he said to them, \q "Food came out of the eater; \q something sweet came out of the strong." \q For three days they could not figure out the answer.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, \q "Katika mlaji kilitoka chakula, \q na katika mwenye nguvu kilitoka [kitu] kitamu." \q Nao hawakuweza kukitegua kitendawili [kwa] siku tatu.
sw.B: Aliwaambia, \q "Kutoka kwa anayekula kilitoka chakula; \q kutoka kwa mwenye nguvu kilitoka kitu kitamu." \q Kwa siku tatu hawakuweza kukitegua kitendawili hicho.
sw.R: Basi aliwaambia, \q "Chakula kilitoka kwa mlaji; \q kitu kitamu kilitoka kwa mwenye nguvu." \q Kwa siku tatu hawakuweza kupata jibu.

es.L: Y les dijo: \q «Del que come salió comida, \q y del fuerte salió [algo] dulce». \q Y no pudieron declarar el enigma [en] tres días.
es.B: Él les dijo: \q «Del que come salió comida; \q del fuerte salió algo dulce». \q Durante tres días no pudieron explicar la adivinanza.
es.R: Entonces les dijo: \q «Del que come salió comida; \q algo dulce salió del fuerte». \q Durante tres días no pudieron encontrar la respuesta.

fr.L: Et il leur dit : \q « De celui qui mange est sortie de la nourriture, \q et du fort est sorti [du] doux. » \q Et ils ne purent pas expliquer l’énigme [pendant] trois jours.
fr.B: Il leur dit : \q « De celui qui mange est sortie de la nourriture ; \q du fort est sortie une douceur. » \q Pendant trois jours, ils ne purent pas expliquer l’énigme.
fr.R: Alors il leur a dit : \q « La nourriture est sortie du mangeur ; \q une douceur est sortie du fort. » \q Pendant trois jours, ils n’ont pas réussi à trouver la réponse.

vi.L: Ông nói với họ: \q "Từ kẻ ăn ra thức ăn, \q và từ kẻ mạnh ra [vật] ngọt." \q Ba ngày họ không giải được câu đố.
vi.B: Ông nói với họ: \q "Từ loài ăn mà ra thức ăn; \q từ loài mạnh mà ra vật ngọt." \q Ba ngày liền họ không giải được câu đố.
vi.R: Vậy ông nói với họ: \q "Thức ăn ra từ kẻ ăn; \q vật ngọt ra từ kẻ mạnh." \q Ba ngày liền họ không tìm ra lời đáp.

ko.L: 그가 그들에게 말했다. \q "먹는 자에게서 먹을 것이 나오고, \q 강한 자에게서 단 것이 나왔다." \q 그들은 사흘 동안 그 수수께끼를 풀지 못하였다.
ko.B: 삼손이 그들에게 말했다. \q "먹는 자에게서 먹을 것이 나오고, \q 강한 자에게서 단 것이 나왔다." \q 그들은 사흘이 지나도록 그 수수께끼를 풀지 못하였다.
ko.R: 그래서 삼손이 그들에게 말했다. \q "먹는 자에게서 먹을 것이 나왔고, \q 강한 자에게서 단 것이 나왔다." \q 그들은 사흘 동안 답을 알아내지 못하였다.

decisions.choice: the riddle: the lion and the honey
decisions.reason: The eater and the strong one are the lion; the food and the sweet thing are the honey (verses 8-9, 18). No one could guess it, because Samson had told no one what happened (verses 6, 9). The riddle is a trap more than a fair puzzle.

decisions.choice: eater ... food: one root
decisions.reason: "Eater" and "food" are from the same root, "eat", and the two lines balance each other: eater and food, strong and sweet. The riddle is set as a short pair of poetic lines.

decisions.choice: three days: they failed for three days
decisions.reason: After three days the companions still had no answer, which leads to their threat in verse 15 (see the note on "seventh day" there).

decisions.choice: the riddle set in two lines
decisions.reason: The riddle is a pair of short poetic lines, so it is set in lines, with the narrative before and after it as separate lines. Readable puts the subject at the start of each line, in plain English order.

decisions.choice: "kẻ ăn" / "loài ăn" and "thức ăn"
decisions.reason: The riddle plays on one Hebrew root for "eater" and "food" (meaning decision); Vietnamese keeps the play with "ăn" in both words.

decisions.choice: "먹는 자" and "먹을 것"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew riddle builds "eater" and "food" from one root; Korean can keep the echo with the one verb "먹다".

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ לְאֵֽשֶׁת־שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ פַּתִּ֣י אֶת־אִישֵׁ֗ךְ וְיַגֶּד־לָ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־הַ֣חִידָ֔ה פֶּן־נִשְׂרֹ֥ף אוֹתָ֛ךְ וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית אָבִ֖יךְ בָּאֵ֑שׁ הַלְיָרְשֵׁ֕נוּ קְרָאתֶ֥ם לָ֖נוּ הֲלֹֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on the seventh day, and they said to [the] wife of Samson, entice your husband, that he tell us the riddle, lest we burn you and the house of your father with fire; to impoverish us did you invite us? [is it] not?

en.L: And it happened on the seventh day that they said to Samson's wife, "Entice your husband, so that he tells us the riddle, or we will burn you and your father's house with fire. Did you invite us to make us poor? Is it not [so]?"
en.B: On the seventh day they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband into telling us the riddle, or we will set fire to you and your father's household. Did you invite us here to rob us? Is that it?"
en.R: On the seventh day they said to Samson's wife, "Trick your husband into telling us the answer to the riddle. If you do not, we will burn you and your father's whole family to death. Did you invite us here just to take everything we own?"

sw.L: Ikawa siku ya saba wakamwambia mke wa Samsoni, "Mshawishi mumeo, ili atuambie kitendawili, tusije tukakuchoma wewe na nyumba ya baba yako kwa moto. Je, mlitualika ili kutufanya maskini? Sivyo?"
sw.B: Siku ya saba walimwambia mke wa Samsoni, "Mbembeleze mumeo atuambie jibu la kitendawili, la sivyo tutakuchoma moto wewe na jamaa ya baba yako. Je, mlitualika hapa ili kutunyang'anya mali? Ndivyo ilivyo?"
sw.R: Siku ya saba walimwambia mke wa Samsoni, "Mdanganye mumeo atuambie jibu la kitendawili. Usipofanya hivyo, tutakuchoma moto wewe na jamaa yote ya baba yako mpaka mfe. Je, mlitualika hapa ili tu kuchukua kila kitu tulicho nacho?"

es.L: Y sucedió al séptimo día que dijeron a la mujer de Sansón: «Persuade a tu marido para que nos declare el enigma, no sea que te quememos a ti y a la casa de tu padre con fuego. ¿Para empobrecernos nos {{plural_you:invitaron|invitasteis}}? ¿No [es así]?».
es.B: Al séptimo día le dijeron a la mujer de Sansón: «Engatusa a tu marido para que nos diga la adivinanza, o te prenderemos fuego a ti y a la familia de tu padre. ¿Nos {{plural_you:invitaron|invitasteis}} aquí para despojarnos? ¿No es eso?».
es.R: Al séptimo día le dijeron a la esposa de Sansón: «Engaña a tu esposo para que te diga la respuesta de la adivinanza. Si no lo haces, te quemaremos viva a ti y a toda la familia de tu padre. ¿Nos {{plural_you:invitaron|invitasteis}} aquí solo para quitarnos todo lo que tenemos?».

fr.L: Et il arriva au septième jour qu’ils dirent à la femme de Samson : « Séduis ton mari, pour qu’il nous explique l’énigme, sinon nous te brûlerons, toi et la maison de ton père, par le feu. Est-ce pour nous dépouiller que vous nous avez invités ? N’[est-ce] pas [cela] ? »
fr.B: Le septième jour, ils dirent à la femme de Samson : « Amène ton mari par la ruse à nous expliquer l’énigme, sinon nous mettrons le feu à toi et à la maison de ton père. Nous avez-vous invités ici pour nous voler ? C’est bien cela ? »
fr.R: Le septième jour, ils ont dit à la femme de Samson : « Trompe ton mari pour qu’il te donne la réponse de la devinette. Sinon, nous vous brûlerons vifs, toi et toute la famille de ton père. Vous nous avez invités ici seulement pour nous prendre tout ce que nous avons ? »

vi.L: Đến ngày thứ bảy, họ nói với vợ của Sam-sôn: "Hãy dụ dỗ chồng cô, để anh ta cho chúng tôi biết câu đố, kẻo chúng tôi lấy lửa đốt cô và nhà cha cô. Có phải các người mời chúng tôi đến để làm cho chúng tôi nghèo đi không? Chẳng phải [thế] sao?"
vi.B: Đến ngày thứ bảy, họ nói với vợ của Sam-sôn: "Hãy dỗ chồng cô nói cho chúng tôi biết câu đố, nếu không chúng tôi sẽ đốt cô và cả nhà cha cô. Các người mời chúng tôi đến đây để cướp của chúng tôi sao? Có phải thế không?"
vi.R: Đến ngày thứ bảy, họ nói với vợ của Sam-sôn: "Hãy lừa chồng cô để anh ta nói cho chúng tôi lời giải của câu đố. Nếu không, chúng tôi sẽ thiêu chết cô và cả nhà cha cô. Các người mời chúng tôi đến đây chỉ để lấy hết của cải chúng tôi sao?"

ko.L: 일곱째 날에 그들이 삼손의 아내에게 말했다. "네 남편을 꾀어서 그 수수께끼를 우리에게 말하게 하여라. 그렇지 않으면 우리가 너와 네 아버지의 집을 불로 태워 버리겠다. 너희가 우리 것을 빼앗으려고 우리를 초대했느냐? 그렇지 않으냐?"
ko.B: 일곱째 날에 그들이 삼손의 아내에게 말했다. "네 남편을 꾀어서 수수께끼의 답을 우리에게 알려 주게 하여라. 그렇지 않으면 너와 네 아버지의 집안을 불태워 버리겠다. 우리 것을 빼앗으려고 우리를 이리 초대했느냐? 그런 것이냐?"
ko.R: 일곱째 날에 그들이 삼손의 아내에게 말했다. "네 남편을 속여서 수수께끼의 답을 알아내어 우리에게 말하여라. 그렇지 않으면 너와 네 아버지의 온 집안을 불태워 죽이겠다. 우리가 가진 것을 모두 빼앗으려고 우리를 여기에 초대한 것이냐?"

decisions.choice: the seventh day
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "the seventh day". The ancient Greek and Syriac translations have "the fourth day", which fits the "three days" of verse 14 and the seven days of weeping in verse 17. The Hebrew is followed here; it may mean that the companions came to her at the last moment, after she had already been weeping over Samson for days.

decisions.choice: entice: persuade by trickery
decisions.reason: The verb means to coax or seduce someone, often by deceit. The Philistine leaders will use the same verb when they set Delilah on Samson (16:5).

decisions.choice: burn you and your father's house with fire
decisions.reason: "Your father's house" is the whole household. The threat is meant literally, and it is later carried out (15:6).

decisions.choice: did you invite us to impoverish us? Is it not so?
alternatives: did you invite us here to impoverish us?
decisions.reason: The verb means to take someone's possessions or make them poor: losing the wager would cost each of them a set of fine clothes. The last two words are a question tag, "is it not?". With a small change of one letter they would read "here": "did you invite us here?"

decisions.choice: invite us here / to rob us / take everything we own
decisions.reason: "Here" is natural English for an invitation and does not decide the question in m4. Balanced says "rob" and Readable says "take everything we own" for "impoverish"; Readable leaves the question tag in the force of the question.

source.text: וַתֵּבְךְּ֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת שִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן עָלָ֗יו וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ רַק־שְׂנֵאתַ֨נִי֙ וְלֹ֣א אֲהַבְתָּ֔נִי הַֽחִידָ֥ה חַ֨דְתָּ֙ לִבְנֵ֣י עַמִּ֔י וְלִ֖י לֹ֣א הִגַּ֑דְתָּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֗הּ הִנֵּ֨ה לְאָבִ֧י וּלְאִמִּ֛י לֹ֥א הִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְלָ֥ךְ אַגִּֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And wept [the] wife of Samson over him, and she said, only you hate me and not you love me; the riddle you have riddled to [the] sons of my people, and to me not you have told [it]. And he said to her, look, to my father and to my mother not I have told, and to you will I tell?

en.L: And Samson's wife wept over him and said, "You only hate me, and you do not love me. You have posed the riddle to the sons of my people, and to me you have not told [it]." And he said to her, "Look, to my father and to my mother I have not told [it], and to you should I tell [it]?"
en.B: Samson's wife wept over him and said, "You only hate me; you do not love me at all. You have given my people a riddle, and you have not told me the answer." He said to her, "Look, I have not told even my father or my mother. Why should I tell you?"
en.R: Samson's wife cried in front of him. "You hate me!" she said. "You do not really love me. You told my people a riddle, but you will not tell me the answer." Samson said to her, "I have not even told my father and mother. Why should I tell you?"

sw.L: Naye mke wa Samsoni akalia mbele yake, akasema, "Wewe unanichukia tu, wala hunipendi. Umewategea wana wa watu wangu kitendawili, nami hujaniambia." Naye akamwambia, "Tazama, baba yangu na mama yangu sijawaambia, nami nikuambie wewe?"
sw.B: Mke wa Samsoni alilia mbele yake, akasema, "Wewe unanichukia tu; hunipendi hata kidogo. Umewategea watu wangu kitendawili, wala hujaniambia jibu lake." Akamwambia, "Tazama, hata baba yangu na mama yangu sijawaambia. Kwa nini nikuambie wewe?"
sw.R: Mke wa Samsoni alilia mbele yake. Alisema, "Unanichukia! Hunipendi kweli. Uliwategea watu wangu kitendawili, lakini hutaki kuniambia jibu." Samsoni alimwambia, "Hata baba yangu na mama yangu sijawaambia. Kwa nini nikuambie wewe?"

es.L: Y la mujer de Sansón lloró sobre él y dijo: «Solamente me aborreces, y no me amas. Has propuesto el enigma a los hijos de mi pueblo, y a mí no me [lo] has declarado». Y él le dijo: «He aquí, a mi padre y a mi madre no [lo] he declarado, ¿y a ti te [lo] declararé?».
es.B: La mujer de Sansón lloró junto a él y le dijo: «Tú solo me odias; no me amas nada. Les has puesto una adivinanza a los de mi pueblo y a mí no me has dicho la respuesta». Él le contestó: «Mira, ni siquiera a mi padre ni a mi madre se lo he dicho. ¿Por qué te lo voy a decir a ti?».
es.R: La esposa de Sansón lloró delante de él. «¡Tú me odias! —le dijo—. En realidad no me amas. Les hiciste una adivinanza a los de mi pueblo, pero no me quieres decir la respuesta». Sansón le dijo: «Ni siquiera se la he dicho a mi padre ni a mi madre. ¿Por qué te la voy a decir a ti?».

fr.L: Et la femme de Samson pleura auprès de lui et dit : « Tu ne fais que me haïr, et tu ne m’aimes pas. Tu as proposé l’énigme aux fils de mon peuple, et à moi tu ne l’as pas expliquée. » Et il lui dit : « Voici, à mon père et à ma mère je ne l’ai pas expliquée, et à toi je l’expliquerais ? »
fr.B: La femme de Samson pleura auprès de lui et dit : « Tu me détestes ; tu ne m’aimes pas du tout. Tu as proposé une énigme aux gens de mon peuple, et tu ne m’as pas dit la réponse. » Il lui répondit : « Écoute, je ne l’ai même pas expliquée à mon père ni à ma mère. Pourquoi te l’expliquerais-je, à toi ? »
fr.R: La femme de Samson s’est mise à pleurer devant lui. « Tu me détestes ! a-t-elle dit. Tu ne m’aimes pas vraiment. Tu as posé une devinette aux gens de mon peuple, mais tu ne veux pas me dire la réponse. » Samson lui a dit : « Je ne l’ai même pas dite à mon père et à ma mère. Pourquoi est-ce que je te la dirais, à toi ? »

vi.L: Vợ Sam-sôn khóc lóc với ông và nói: "Anh chỉ ghét em, chứ không yêu em. Anh đã ra câu đố cho con cái dân tộc em, mà không cho em biết." Ông nói với nàng: "Này, ngay cả cha mẹ anh, anh cũng chưa cho biết, thì anh lại nói cho em sao?"
vi.B: Vợ Sam-sôn khóc lóc với ông: "Anh chỉ ghét em, chứ chẳng yêu em chút nào. Anh ra câu đố cho người dân tộc em mà không cho em biết lời giải." Ông nói với nàng: "Này, ngay cả cha mẹ anh, anh cũng chưa nói. Sao anh lại phải nói cho em?"
vi.R: Vợ Sam-sôn khóc lóc trước mặt ông. Nàng nói: "Anh ghét em! Anh không thật lòng yêu em. Anh ra câu đố cho người dân tộc em, mà anh không chịu cho em biết lời giải." Sam-sôn nói với nàng: "Ngay cả cha mẹ anh, anh cũng chưa nói. Sao anh phải nói cho em?"

ko.L: 삼손의 아내가 그의 앞에서 울며 말했다. "당신은 나를 미워할 뿐이고 사랑하지 않아요. 당신이 내 백성의 자손들에게 수수께끼를 내고서 나에게는 말해 주지 않았어요." 삼손이 그 여자에게 말했다. "보시오, 내 아버지와 어머니에게도 말하지 않았는데, 당신에게 말하겠소?"
ko.B: 삼손의 아내가 그의 앞에서 울며 말했다. "당신은 나를 미워할 뿐이에요. 나를 조금도 사랑하지 않아요. 당신은 내 동족에게 수수께끼를 내 놓고, 나에게는 그 답을 말해 주지 않았어요." 삼손이 그 여자에게 말했다. "보시오, 나는 내 아버지와 어머니에게도 말하지 않았소. 그런데 왜 당신에게 말해야 하오?"
ko.R: 삼손의 아내가 그의 앞에서 울었다. 그 여자가 말했다. "당신은 나를 미워해요! 당신은 나를 정말로 사랑하지 않아요. 우리 사람들에게 수수께끼를 내 놓고, 나에게는 답을 말해 주지 않잖아요." 삼손이 그 여자에게 말했다. "나는 아버지와 어머니에게도 말하지 않았소. 왜 내가 당신에게 말해야 하오?"

decisions.choice: you only hate me, you do not love me
decisions.reason: She puts it as sharply as she can: his silence proves he does not love her. Delilah will press him in almost the same words (16:15).

decisions.choice: the sons of my people: her countrymen
decisions.reason: The phrase means the men of her own people, the thirty companions. She sets them against herself: he has shared a riddle with them, but will not share its answer with his wife.

decisions.choice: to my father and to my mother ... and to you?
decisions.reason: Samson puts his parents first for emphasis: he has kept the secret even from them, so why should he tell her? His answer treats her as an outsider, which is how she has just accused him of treating her.

decisions.choice: my people
decisions.reason: "Sons of my people" is an idiom for her countrymen; Balanced and Readable say "my people".

decisions.choice: Samson and his wife say "anh" and "em"
decisions.reason: As the Genesis note sets for husband and wife.

decisions.choice: Samson's wife speaks to him in the polite informal style (해요체); Samson answers her in the 하오체 with "당신"
decisions.reason: Husband and wife speak with mutual respect, as the terms set; Samson's 하오체 is a little firmer and older-sounding, which suits his refusal. A reviewer may prefer 해요체 for both.

source.text: וַתֵּ֤בְךְּ עָלָיו֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וַיַּגֶּד־לָהּ֙ כִּ֣י הֱצִיקַ֔תְהוּ וַתַּגֵּ֥ד הַחִידָ֖ה לִבְנֵ֥י עַמָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she wept over him the seven days which was to them the feast; and it was on the seventh day, and he told her, for she pressed him, and she told the riddle to [the] sons of her people.

en.L: And she wept over him the seven days that the feast lasted for them, and it happened on the seventh day that he told her, because she pressed him hard, and she told the riddle to the sons of her people.
en.B: She wept over him all through the seven days of their feast. On the seventh day he told her, because she kept pressing him, and she explained the riddle to her people.
en.R: She cried in front of him for the whole seven days of the feast. On the seventh day he finally told her, because she kept begging him. Then she told the answer to her people.

sw.L: Naye akalia mbele yake zile siku saba ambazo karamu yao ilidumu; ikawa siku ya saba akamwambia, kwa sababu alimsumbua sana; naye akawaambia wana wa watu wake kitendawili.
sw.B: Alilia mbele yake siku zote saba za karamu yao. Siku ya saba alimwambia, kwa sababu aliendelea kumsumbua, naye akawaeleza watu wake jibu la kitendawili.
sw.R: Alilia mbele yake kwa siku zote saba za karamu. Siku ya saba hatimaye alimwambia, kwa sababu aliendelea kumsihi. Kisha yeye akawaambia watu wake jibu.

es.L: Y lloró sobre él los siete días que les duró el banquete; y sucedió al séptimo día que él se lo declaró, porque lo había presionado; y ella declaró el enigma a los hijos de su pueblo.
es.B: Ella estuvo llorando junto a él durante los siete días del banquete. Al séptimo día él se lo dijo, porque ella no dejaba de presionarlo, y ella les explicó la adivinanza a los de su pueblo.
es.R: Ella lloró delante de él durante los siete días del banquete. Al séptimo día, por fin, él se lo dijo, porque ella no dejaba de rogarle. Entonces ella les dio la respuesta a los de su pueblo.

fr.L: Et elle pleura auprès de lui les sept jours que dura pour eux le festin ; et il arriva au septième jour qu’il la lui expliqua, parce qu’elle le pressait, et elle expliqua l’énigme aux fils de son peuple.
fr.B: Elle pleura auprès de lui pendant les sept jours de leur festin. Le septième jour, il la lui expliqua, parce qu’elle ne cessait de le harceler, et elle expliqua l’énigme aux gens de son peuple.
fr.R: Elle a pleuré devant lui pendant les sept jours du festin. Le septième jour, il a fini par lui donner la réponse, parce qu’elle n’arrêtait pas de le supplier. Ensuite elle a donné la réponse aux gens de son peuple.

vi.L: Nàng khóc lóc với ông suốt bảy ngày tiệc của họ; đến ngày thứ bảy ông nói cho nàng biết, vì nàng nài ép ông, và nàng nói câu đố cho con cái dân tộc mình.
vi.B: Nàng khóc lóc với ông suốt bảy ngày tiệc. Đến ngày thứ bảy, vì nàng cứ nài ép, ông nói cho nàng biết, và nàng giải thích câu đố cho người dân tộc mình.
vi.R: Nàng khóc lóc trước mặt ông suốt bảy ngày tiệc. Đến ngày thứ bảy, cuối cùng ông nói cho nàng biết, vì nàng cứ năn nỉ mãi. Rồi nàng nói lời giải cho người dân tộc mình.

ko.L: 그들이 잔치하는 이레 동안 그 여자가 그의 앞에서 울었다. 일곱째 날에 그 여자가 그를 몹시 졸랐으므로 그가 그 여자에게 말해 주었다. 그러자 그 여자는 자기 백성의 자손들에게 그 수수께끼를 말해 주었다.
ko.B: 그 여자는 잔치가 계속되는 이레 내내 그의 앞에서 울었다. 그 여자가 계속 조르자, 일곱째 날에 삼손은 그 답을 말해 주었다. 그러자 그 여자는 그 수수께끼의 답을 자기 동족에게 알려 주었다.
ko.R: 그 여자는 잔치가 열린 이레 동안 내내 삼손 앞에서 울었다. 그 여자가 계속 조르자, 일곱째 날에 삼손은 마침내 답을 말해 주었다. 그러자 그 여자는 그 답을 자기 사람들에게 알려 주었다.

decisions.choice: the seven days: through the feast
decisions.reason: She wept through the whole feast. With "the seventh day" in verse 15, this means she was already weeping before the companions threatened her; see the note there.

decisions.choice: she pressed him: she wore him down
decisions.reason: The verb means to press hard, to harass. It is used again when Delilah wears Samson down (16:16).

decisions.choice: she told the riddle: she told its answer
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, "tell" a riddle means give its answer.

decisions.choice: kept pressing / finally / kept begging
decisions.reason: The verb describes pressure over time; Balanced and Readable show that with "kept", and Readable adds "finally".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לוֹ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י בְּטֶ֨רֶם֙ יָבֹ֣א הַחַ֔רְסָה מַה־מָּת֣וֹק מִדְּבַ֔שׁ וּמֶ֥ה עַ֖ז מֵאֲרִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם לוּלֵא֙ חֲרַשְׁתֶּ֣ם בְּעֶגְלָתִ֔י לֹ֥א מְצָאתֶ֖ם חִידָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him [the] men of the city on the seventh day before went the sun, what [is] sweeter than honey, and what [is] stronger than a lion? And he said to them, if not you had plowed with my heifer, not you would have found out my riddle.
